control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with calm curiosity, unhurried and articulate.
target_text: This is what the world looks like when humans live to one hundred and fifty. And no, it isn't a world of very old people. It's a world where nobody leaves. By the end, you'll see why, in this world, the healthiest mother on the street is her children's biggest problem.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with gently rising interest, as the pieces connect.
target_text: It starts quietly. One morning, ageing slows down, for everyone, from wherever their body already is. A man blows out forty candles, same as last year.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with steady, curious momentum, one step leading to the next.
target_text: He'll now make it to about a hundred and thirty. His father, who's seventy, gets twenty-odd bonus years. And the baby born in the hospital across town that morning? She's the first human who will ever see one hundred and fifty.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with a shade more energy, following the chain forward.
target_text: Across town, at a pension company, someone changes one number on a spreadsheet. Eighty becomes one hundred and fifty. Every cell below it turns red.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with quiet, unhurried weight, each word placed with care.
target_text: Because here's the thing we never notice. The whole world is built around people leaving.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with calm perspective, letting the moment land.
target_text: You work for about forty years, then you stop. Your parents pass away, and in your fifties, you get the house. The boss retires, and somebody gets promoted. Every few decades, the jobs, the homes, the money and the power all come free again. Death is the thing that moves the queue.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with a touch softer and slower, without melodrama.
target_text: Take that away, and the queue stops moving. And the first place you notice is the family photo.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with calm, deadpan restraint, the punchline already clear.
target_text: Today, a big family photo has three rows. Grandparents at the back, parents in the middle, kids on the floor. In this world, you retake it every twenty years, and every time, the frame gets wider. By the time that baby from the hospital is a great-great-grandmother, it's five rows deep. Five generations, all alive, all healthy, all arguing about where to sit.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with matter-of-fact warmth, noticing the absurd without fuss.
target_text: And look at the front row. It's almost empty.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with light, amused understatement, unhurried.
target_text: If everyone lives twice as long and keeps having kids at today's pace, the planet runs out of room. So families shrink. The world grows to about nineteen billion people, roughly double today, and then it stops. Children go from one in every four people to one in eight.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with dry, understated delivery, letting the details do the work.
target_text: A kid in this world is rare. She is outnumbered by her own ancestors at her own birthday party.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with calm curiosity, unhurried and articulate.
target_text: And if the family photo gets longer, so does the marriage in the middle of it. Today, "till death do us part" means about fifty years. Here, marry at thirty, and death is a hundred and twenty years away. That's a very long time to agree on a thermostat.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with gently rising interest, as the pieces connect.
target_text: So the vows change. Couples start writing an end date into them. At the jeweller's, wedding rings come engraved with a year, the way milk comes with a date. And Grandma's third wedding is a lovely day. Her first husband gives a speech.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with steady, curious momentum, one step leading to the next.
target_text: Longer marriages are a choice. Longer careers aren't.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with a shade more energy, following the chain forward.
target_text: Today, you start work at twenty, stop at sixty-five, and have about fifteen years left. Here, stopping at sixty-five would leave you eighty-five years with no pay. control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with calm curiosity, unhurried and articulate.
target_text: Picture your first payslip at twenty. Near the bottom, a new line: years to retirement, ninety-four.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with gently rising interest, as the pieces connect.
target_text: But a hundred-year career has a problem. Whatever you learned at twenty is useless by sixty. So people go back to school, again and again. In a lecture hall, a seventy-year-old sits next to an eighteen-year-old.

target_text: And a hundred years of work means a hundred years of paying for a home. You'd think time would make everyone rich. control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with matter-of-fact warmth, noticing the absurd without fuss.
target_text: So people borrow instead, and the banks invent the hundred-year mortgage. It sounds cheap. It isn't.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with light, amused understatement, unhurried.
target_text: On a three hundred thousand dollar house, the monthly payment drops by less than three hundred dollars. But you pay three and a half times as much interest. You're not really paying off the house. You're renting it from the bank, for the rest of your very long life.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with dry, understated delivery, letting the details do the work.
target_text: A letter arrives. Payment eight hundred and forty-seven of one thousand, two hundred.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with a shade more energy, following the chain forward.
target_text: Which is why everyone is waiting for the other way to get a house. The one you inherit.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with steady, curious momentum, one step leading to the next.
target_text: Not one of them has changed hands in ninety years. Today, about one home in forty-five comes free each year when somebody dies. Here, it's one in a hundred and fifteen. And there are twice as many people who need one.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with a shade more energy, following the chain forward.
target_text: A brass key hangs inside one of those doors. It has a paper tag, for writing each owner's name. It's had one name on it for a very long time.

target_text: So the young do something clever, and a little bit dark. At twenty-five, they sell their future inheritance to a bank, for cash today. The bank now owns the right to Mum's house. And every year, on Mum's birthday, the bank sends her a card. It asks how she's feeling.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with measured seriousness, a little tighter and steadier.
target_text: The same queue that blocks the front door blocks the top floor. On the fortieth floor of the Greyfield Exchange, the desk nameplates are engraved in brass. Nobody prints them anymore. Nobody has moved desks in eighty years.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with focused, low-register restraint, deliberate and steady.
target_text: The same goes for judges, for professors, for anyone who holds a seat until they choose to leave. In a courthouse hallway, six portraits hang side by side. It's the same judge. Each one is a little greyer.

target_text: So ambition leaves. If you can't climb the old ladder, you build a new one. Every founder is under forty, because only a brand new company has no queue. And the one thing young people vote for, over and over, is term limits. On everything.

target_text: Now, to be fair, some of this is wonderful. A surgeon with ninety years of practice. A teacher who taught your grandmother, and now teaches you, and still remembers what your grandmother was like at your age. Longer lives have always made the world richer. That part is true.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with gently rising interest, as the pieces connect.
target_text: And then there's death itself. It doesn't vanish. It changes shape.

control_instruction: Engaging video essay storyteller, curious and articulate. Speaks with steady, curious momentum, one step leading to the next.
